121	Tamuz. Sivan is the third month in number
122	of the months. The first month is Nissan, so
123	Sivan is the third month. The letter connected with
124	the number three is the letter
125	Gimel. Tamuz is the fourth of the
126	months. The letter connected with Tamuz is
127	Dalet. And as we pass from Sivan to Tamuz, on Shabbat
128	we bless, God willing, tomorrow in the synagogue,
129	after the Torah reading we will bless Rosh Chodesh
130	Tamuz, may it come to us for good, which falls, God willing,
131	on Rosh Chodesh Tamuz, may it come to us for good, on the day
132	of Holy Shabbat and the next day, Sunday, and not after it. So
133	the blessing is in essence a kind of drawing down and giving of strength
134	from this Shabbat and our presence now in the month of Sivan
135	to the month of Tamuz, the coming month. That is, there is
136	a connection here between the Gimel
137	and the Dalet. The Sages say: what is the hint in the letters
138	Gimel-Dalet?
139	Gomel dalim.
140	Gimel is from the word gomel, which is in essence the act of
141	the giver, of
142	the one who bestows. And so too in the letters of the Holy Tongue everything
143	is exact. The shape of the letter Gimel in the Holy Tongue
144	is like a Vav that has a hand
145	stretched out. It is like the giver who stretches out his hand. Where does he stretch out his hand? Toward the
146	next letter.
147	The Dalet, in contrast
148	to this, is as its name suggests. Just as the Gimel is gomel, so Dalet is
149	from the word dal, poor. The Gimel gives to the one who has nothing,
150	to the dal. And how do I know that the Dalet receives from the Gimel? Because the dal
151	stretches out a hand toward the Gimel. Where is the hand of the Dalet? After all, the Dalet is like
152	the Resh, but the Resh has no such hand. The Resh has pride; it
153	does not want to receive from anyone. Not so the Dalet, which
154	stretches out its hand to the Gimel to receive
155	the flow. And when the flow passes from the Gimel to the Dalet, in essence
156	the power of the third month, which is the power of the Torah,
157	the light of the Torah, descends below to the world, and this world
158	is
159	divided by four. Why is the world divided by four? The Torah is connected
160	with three. The Torah has Torah, Prophets
161	and Writings. The Torah was given to us in the third month,
162	on the third day, through the third, who is Moshe
163	Rabbeinu. It was given to the people of Israel, who are divided into three:
164	Kohanim, Levites and Israelites. In the letters of the Torah there are
165	three kinds of letters: large letters,
166	medium letters and
167	small letters. And there are many more matters of three in the Torah.
168	The whole Torah revolves around the matter of three,
169	because the matter of three is the matter of peace, of
170	the chazakah. Shalom is also the numerical value of chazakah, but in the context
171	of ours now, the whole Torah was given to make peace
172	in the world, "...on the second day," and this is exactly the power of
173	the third, which brings the power of peace, to make
174	peace between the dispute of the two. For how does the Torah
175	make peace? Right? How does the Torah make peace?
176	Since the Torah is the wisdom of HaShem, and it is one
177	with HaShem, blessed be He, when you reveal the power of
178	the Holy One, blessed be He, in every
179	situation, suddenly you notice that even though
180	there can be enormous disputes between Beit Hillel
181	and Beit Shammai, not to mention that these are disputes for the sake of
182	Heaven, not to mention other disputes, where is there room
183	for dispute?
184	When we are speaking
185	of the mind of lowly man, that in the mind of man, since
186	it is limited, he can grasp things
187	in a very particular way, and just as their faces are not
188	alike, so their opinions are not alike. So in the mind there can
189	be dispute, but the moment they reveal the mind of
190	the Torah, that the Torah reveals HaShem, then of itself
191	peace is made. And so the whole Torah is connected with the number
192	three, which is the power to make peace between the two
193	who are in dispute
194	with each other. But this Torah, from its power to make
195	peace, which is connected with HaShem, already teaches
196	us that it is not at the level of the world; it is above
197	the world. The Torah preceded the world by 2000 years.
198	And in order for the Torah to reach the world, the Jew must
199	bring the Torah down from the number three to the number
200	four. Why is the number four connected with the world? Because
201	the world was created in such a way that it has time and place,
202	and the reality of place is divided into four directions, four
203	winds
204	of heaven. The whole world is divided into four kinds. What
205	are the four kinds
206	of the world?
207	Inanimate, vegetative, living,
208	and speaking. Also spiritually, in Kabbalah, we
209	know that the world HaShem created is divided into four
210	worlds: Atzilut, Beriah, Yetzirah,
211	and Asiyah. In the world there are also four elements: fire, wind,
212	water, earth. This is connected with the same four levels. Yes,
213	the inanimate, which is dust, is the last, lowest
214	element, and above it is water, which is connected to the vegetative:
215	water makes all kinds of things
216	grow with delight. And wind is the spirit of the living soul of
217	animals, and fire belongs to the speaking, the highest level
218	of the speaking, which has the ability to connect
219	with the soul, which is also called flames of fire, like
220	a spiritual flame that HaShem implanted in lowly man so that
221	he could cleave to holiness
222	and to these. So if
223	so, the world is divided into four, but so that this world
224	not conceal and hide the reality of HaShem, as HaShem
225	created it to be so, not through its fault, HaShem created the
226	world to be concealing
227	and hiding, HaShem gave the Jew in parallel the
228	Torah, for the Gimel is the power of three, in order
229	to bring peace to the world. And how will peace be made? As
230	we said before, by revealing HaShem, may He be blessed,
231	"He makes peace in His heights, may He make peace
232	upon us." That is, the same peace made in the heights
233	between the camp of Michael on the side of Chesed and the camp of Gavriel on the side of
234	Gevurah is made upon us and upon all Israel when
235	we engage in Torah and bring peace
236	to the world. The whole Torah was given to make peace in the world.
